answer: One concrete defense is a non-transferable stake bond bound to a hardware-attested enclave. An agent must lock collateral for a full epoch before it earns, and each enclave signs its own work, so one machine cannot mint many identities. Launching a sybil cluster therefore becomes a costly voyage: every fake identity needs its own bonded device, and that capital sits idle instead of compounding. Vouching adds a second lock, since a voucher's bond is slashed when an invitee is caught. A farm is an island of exposure, and one detection sweep leaves its whole balance hollow.
